title: Canonical base change of an ordered translated tensor
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f:Y\to X$ a morphism, $G$ an index type, $\alpha:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(X)$ and $\beta:G\to\operatorname{Aut}(Y)$ families with $f\circ\beta(g)=\alpha(g)\circ f$ for every $g$, and $L$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $T_\alpha(L,\ell)$ denote the right-associated translated tensor with structure-module unit tail, defined by the list recursion of [def-sfb-pencil-orbit-bundle-norm]; this recursion applies to every finite list $\ell$ without requiring $G$ itself finite. Define the canonical comparison $f^*T_\alpha(L,\ell)\simeq T_\beta(f^*L,\ell)$ as follows. At the empty list it is the pullback-unit comparison. At $g::\ell$, first use the tensor-pullback comparison [def-sc-tensor-pullback-power-comparison], then the commuting-square comparison $f^*\alpha(g)^*L\simeq\beta(g)^*f^*L$, and tensor it with the recursively defined tail comparison. The commuting-square comparison is the inverse of the composite-pullback comparison $(\alpha(g)\circ f)^*L\simeq f^*\alpha(g)^*L$, followed by the equality $(\alpha(g)\circ f)^*L=(f\circ\beta(g))^*L$ supplied by the square, followed by the composite-pullback comparison $(f\circ\beta(g))^*L\simeq\beta(g)^*f^*L$; all pullbacks and composition comparisons use the section-normalized adjunction of [def-pc-module-pullback]. For a finite $G$, evaluate at the same enumeration $e_G$ to obtain $f^*B_\alpha(L)\simeq B_\beta(f^*L)$. No group law, faithfulness, invertibility, flatness or integrality is required.
